intro_line: Managua: gritty capital where volcanoes and lake breezes meet.
intro: Managua rewards visitors who look past its rough edges to find markets, lakefront life and easy trips to volcanoes and colonial towns. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
transit_facts: No metro or tram; travel is by bus, taxi or car.
City buses are numbered, cheap (about C$2.50) and stop early; no night service.
Bus 266 runs from Mercado Oriental to the airport along Carretera Norte.
Taxis are collective or private; agree the fare first. No Uber.
Ride apps are limited; arrange taxis by phone or hotel.
Driving is congested and addresses use landmarks, not street numbers.
Walking is possible downtown and at Puerto Salvador Allende; cycling is for the bold.

airports.name: Augusto C. Sandino International Airport
airports.note: Main international gateway, about 8 km east of the centre.

options.note: Walk out to Carretera Norte to catch it; watch for the terminal on your right.
Ask the driver to stop at the airport.
Agree the fare before you get in.
Book ahead through your hotel for safety.
